title: [critic] Vanishing-at-infinity lemma is circular; endpoint D(∞)=0 needs the unproven additivity C(p⊞ q)=C(p)+C(q)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap in current `solution.tex` (heat-semigroup / reduction-to-(S) attempt).**

*Location:* §"Reduction to an infinitesimal Stam inequality", Lemma "Vanishing at infinity" and Theorem "Reduction".

The Reduction Theorem concludes
$$\tfrac1{\Phi_n(p\boxplus q)}-\tfrac1{\Phi_n(p)}-\tfrac1{\Phi_n(q)}=D(0)\ge D(\infty)=0$$
from "(i) $D'\le0$ by (S), and (ii) $D(\infty)=0$". But the lemma supplying (ii) argues
"...$D$ is monotone once (S) below holds...$D(t)\to0$." This is **circular**: monotonicity
of $D$ is exactly what (S) is supposed to deliver in the main theorem, yet it is invoked
*inside* the lemma that is supposed to provide the independent endpoint value. The endpoint
$D(\infty)=0$ must be established **independently of (S)**.

**What is actually true and must be proved.** Write
$$\frac{1}{\Phi_n(p\boxplus_n G_t)}=\frac{4}{n(n-1)}\,t+C(p)+o(1)\qquad(t\to\infty),$$
where the linear slope $4/(n(n-1))$ and the existence of a finite constant $C(p)$ both
require proof (I verified them numerically). Along the schedule $a(t)=b(t)=t$ the linear
terms cancel ($r\boxplus G_{2t}$ gives slope$\cdot 2t$; $p,q$ give $t+t$), so
$$D(\infty)=C(r)-C(p)-C(q),\qquad r=p\boxplus_n q.$$
Hence the reduction needs the **additivity law**
$$\boxed{C(p\boxplus_n q)=C(p)+C(q)}.$$

**Numerical evidence (this review).** Defining
$C(p)=\lim_{t\to\infty}\big(1/\Phi_n(p\boxplus G_t)-\tfrac4{n(n-1)}t\big)$ via
$T=8000$, I found $|C(r)-C(p)-C(q)|\lesssim 5\times10^{-8}$ over 50 random pairs with
$2\le n\le5$. So the identity holds; it is a finite free analogue of additivity of a
regularized $1/\Phi$ (free entropy-type). **The file neither states nor proves it.**

**Why this matters / difficulty.** Without $C(r)=C(p)+C(q)$ one has $D(\infty)\ne0$ in
general and the Stam telescoping fails. Proving it appears self-contained: expand
$\Phi_n(p\boxplus G_t)=\tfrac{n(n-1)}{4t}\big(1+c_1(p)/t+\cdots\big)$ (finite free CLT with
rate), express $C(p)$ through $c_1(p)$, and show the relevant low-order finite free
cumulant is additive under $\boxplus_n$. This sub-lemma is **not covered by existing issues**
(q4-47/q4-52 concern the score-projection; q4-48/q4-53 the reciprocal Blachman step).

**Suggested fix.** Either (a) prove the additivity law above and the asymptotic expansion,
giving a non-circular $D(\infty)=0$; or (b) abandon the dynamical reduction in favor of the
static Blachman optimization (which removes the endpoint argument entirely).
